question: Which statement is FALSE regarding Brokered CDs?
choices: These instruments have a limited trading market
There is a penalty for early withdrawal
There can be a loss of principal upon an early withdrawal
There is FDIC insurance on these products as long as the CD is titled in the customer's name
explanation: If interest rates rise after issuance, the value of the CD in the secondary market will fall (though not by much, since this is a short maturity). There is no penalty for early withdrawal of funds on brokered CDs - however the amount of interest earned will be pro-rated over the shorter life of the deposit. Most of these instruments are held to maturity, so the secondary market is very limited. Brokered CDs qualify for FDIC insurance as long as the CD is titled in the customer's name.

question: Bonds issued by states, cities, and counties, school districts, highway departments, and other public authorities are known as:
explanation: Municipal bonds are used to fund specific public projects, including projects related to public education, highway construction, sports and event stadiums and arenas, and mass transit. They are generally exempt from taxes by the federal government, and sometimes state and local governments.

question: Trades of municipal bonds settle "regular way" on:
explanation: Trades of municipal securities settle "regular way" 1 business day after trade date. Note that "T" is the abbreviation for trade date.

question: Feasibility studies are most likely to be performed in conjunction with what?
explanation: Revenue bonds are bonds that finance projects in which principal and interest payments to the bondholder are paid from the revenue generated by those projects. Unlike GO bonds there is no government or taxpayer guarantee insuring that a revenue bond will be repaid, therefore a feasibility study is a valuable component of a revenue bond's issuance. Treasury bonds are issued by the US Treasury for general government purposes, and they are backed by the tax-paying authority of the US government. James Bond, also known as Agent 007, is a fictional character created by author Ian Fleming.

question: The proceeds of a "Build America Bond" may be used for all of the following EXCEPT:
explanation: Build America Bonds (BABs) were issued by municipalities in 2009 and 2010. They are taxable municipal bonds that get a 35% Federal interest rate subsidy and the bond proceeds must be used for capital improvements (this is part of the economic stimulus program after the 2008-2009 "great recession"). These bonds were meant to create jobs and make it easier for municipalities to access the debt market for needed capital projects. The proceeds of BABs cannot be used to prerefund existing issues (that does not create jobs).

explanation: Trades of municipal securities settle "regular way" 1 business day after the trade date.

question: What type of municipal bond is backed by the full faith and credit of the issuer?
explanation:
Municipal general obligation bonds are backed by the full faith and credit of the issuer, as well as the issuer's taxing power. General obligation bonds issued by local units of government often are payable from the issuer's ad valorem taxes, while general obligation bonds issued by states often are payable from appropriations made by the state legislature.
Revenue bonds are backed by a pledge of revenues from an enterprise activity or from a taxing source other than ad valorem taxes (e.g., sales or excise taxes). Mortgage bonds are corporate bonds issued by utilities, where a mortgage on all of the property, plant and generating equipment of the utility backs the bond issue. A credit enhanced municipal bond applies a bank letter of credit to the bond issue, improving the bond's rating (the bank will pay if the municipality cannot).

source.name: Chapter 5 Test: Municipal Debt and Money Market Instruments

question: Which of the following is not true of money market instruments?
choices: They are typically issued at a discount to par
explanation:
Money market instruments are debt obligations that mature in one year or less. The short maturity of these securities enables them to be easily turned into cash. They are also very safe and therefore offer low yields. Longer-term debt obligations are called capital market instruments because they are a source of long-term capital for the issuer.
Money market obligations are traded in large units ($1,000,000 or $5,000,000 minimum) between institutions. Typically, they are issued at a discount to par value and mature at par, with any gain treated as interest income.

source.name: Chapter 5 Test: Municipal Debt and Money Market Instruments

question: Which statement is TRUE about a Certificate of Participation (COP)?
choices: COPs are subject to statutory debt limits
COPs are backed by a pledge of lease revenues
COPs have a higher credit rating than G.O. bonds of the same issuer
COPs are full faith and credit obligations of the issuer
explanation:
As municipalities reached their debt limits with G.O. bond issuance, they found it harder and harder to get voter approval to raise limits to sell additional G.O. bonds (think of Proposition 13 in California that capped property taxes to almost no increase unless the property was sold). To get around this, the COP - Certificate of Participation - was invented and COP issuance is now greater than G.O. bond issuance in many states.
A COP is issued by a state entity where lease revenues are pledged to back the issue. The lease payments are received from a project such as a university dormitory, prison, municipal office building, municipal transit system, etc. The "difference" is that the lease payment is made based on the governing body making an annual appropriation from tax collections, and it is not "legally" obligated to do so, hence it is not really a bond. Rather, it is a security that gives the holder a share of "revenue" if the appropriation is made (which it will be, otherwise that issuer's credit rating would be trashed).
COP issuance has increased greatly over the years because they are easier to issue than G.O. debt (no pesky debt limits or voter approval to deal with) - but they are sold at a slightly higher yield, because they have more credit risk.

question: Which statement is TRUE regarding debt obligations?
choices: Revenue bonds are backed by the full faith and credit of the issuing municipality
explanation: Corporations issue income bonds (also known as adjustment bonds) in times of corporate distress. These bonds obligate the issuer to pay only if the issuer has sufficient income. Municipalities issue revenue bonds, which pledge the revenues from a facility (such as a bridge or tunnel) to pay for the debt service on the bond issue - not the full faith and credit of the issuer.

source.name: Chapter 5 Test: Municipal Debt and Money Market Instruments

question: Which of these municipal securities is backed by the full faith and credit of the municipality?
explanation: G.O. bonds are issued to fund the general operating expenses of the municipal government or to provide funds for capital improvement projects, such as roads, parks, courthouses, and schools. They are backed by the full faith and credit of the issuer, which means that the municipality must use its full taxing and borrowing authority to ensure the timely payment of principal and interest.

question: Municipalities would issue tax exempt commercial paper for all of the following reasons EXCEPT to:
choices: meet a temporary cash shortage due to unforeseen extraordinary expenses
provide construction period financing that will be permanently financed by a future bond sale
smooth out collections of funds that are normally subject to seasonal fluctuations
explanation: Most municipalities finance short term needs through BANs (Bond Anticipation Notes), TANs (Tax Anticipation Notes), RANs (Revenue Anticipation Notes) and TRANs (Tax and Revenue Anticipation Notes). However, commercial paper could be used by a municipality to finance short term cash shortages caused by slow tax collections or unforeseen extraordinary expenses (these could also be financed by tax anticipation notes). Also, commercial paper could be used for an interim construction loan, because when a building is under construction, the long term financing may not yet be in place (of course, the municipality could also finance the construction through a bond anticipation note). Commercial paper cannot be used for long term financing such as a bond refunding.

question: In order for municipal bond investors to receive the state tax exemption on their interest payments, it is necessary that they:
choices: invest in bonds with at least a BBB rating
live in the state in which the municipality issuing the bonds exists
explanation: In order for municipal bond interest to be exempt from taxation at the state level, the investor must live in the same state as the issuing municipality. For example, only Kansas residents will get state-tax free income from a Kansas municipal bond.

question: Which of the following typically mature in less than a year?
explanation: Commercial paper is a term for short-term debt issued by corporations and municipalities. Commercial paper typically matures in under 270 days. Treasury notes have maturities of 2-10 years, and mortgage-backed securities are also longer-term securities. Auction rate securities are often treated as short-term investments; however, this is because their interest rates reset periodically and not because they have a short time to maturity when first issued.

question: CDs are all of the following, except:
choices: Instruments that allow bank, savings and loan, and credit union customers to receive higher interest on their deposits than a savings or checking account
Investments that include Bank CDs, Brokered CDs, brokered long-term CDs, negotiable CDs, and jumbo CDs
explanation: Certificates of deposit (CDs) are used when customers wish to obtain higher returns than in a savings account. The customer agrees to tie up their money for a fixed period, which can range from one month to five years, in exchange for a higher yield.
